newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NZ stowaways discovered in Australian outback.
newsitem.headline: NZ stowaways discovered in Australian outback.

text.p: Two New Zealand stowaways who went missing after jumping from a Malaysian container ship last month were found alive and well in the remote Australian outback on Wednesday by a group of local Aborigines, police said.
The two, 21-year-old twin sisters Sarah and Joanne Ingham, jumped ship with a 27-year-old sailor off Princess Charlotte Bay in the far north of Queensland state three weeks ago.
The trio, wearing lifejackets, drifted ashore through shark- and crocodile-infested waters, prompting a large, unsuccessful air-and-sea search.
But they were found on Wednesday by members of a remote Aboriginal community around 50 kms (30 miles) inland at Coen in the Cape York Peninsula.
A spokesman for Coen police told reporters he believed the trio had survived once they reached the shore by eating oysters and crabs from the bay.
Aborgines had then shown them the way inland to Coen, the spokesman said. After being found in Coen they were taken to Cairns for questioning by police and immigration officials.

Ian Swan of Cairns police told reporters the twins stowed away on February 5 when the ship was docked in New Zealand and were discovered on April 14 as the ship was en route from Singapore to Auckland.
"(The women) boarded at the invitation of the seaman and when they woke up they found themselves at sea," Swan said.
The Ingham sisters and crew member Ja'afar Bin Mohamed Zan disappeared several days after they were discovered by the captain of the container vessel Bunga Teresek.
Fears for the trio's safety mounted when three lifejackets were found to be missing while the ship was en route from Singapore to Brisbane.
The twins' mother said in a television interview from New Zealand she was ecstatic at the news her daughters were safe.
"I'm over the moon, it's the best Mother's Day present I could ever have," Jeanette Ingham said.
